exception.reason: The strongest direction—Latin American histories, societies and political economy—was tested before language/migration/identity and literature/film/popular-culture directions. UCR provides relevant general methods in history, sociology, politics, international relations, economics, public policy, linguistics, literature and media. With one limited Latin American civil-repair case in a sociology course, the current catalogue does not provide a sustained Latin America-specific sequence, Spanish or Portuguese language study, or enough regional cultural content to organise 23 non-PPD courses. Turning the strongest generic courses into a global politics, colonial studies, cognitive-language or media programme would shift away from the target-specific interests rather than supply a complete related response. The conclusion rests on actual content and regional coherence, not title matching, exact module equivalence, study-abroad logistics or professional qualification.
exception.curriculumContext: The settled Spanish pathway remains complete at 180 EC. It preserves 30 EC of Spanish study, the Latin America-specific history, indigeneity, sociolinguistics, culture, international-relations, policy and capstone components, the required approved 30-EC Latin America study-abroad package, and 30 EC of genuine open choice. Spanish is the selected broad-regional option rather than a universal requirement, and no unverified host units or alternative Portuguese/Brazil route is invented. No first-stage curriculum decision is reopened.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions or outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and the six cohort availability columns. GOSHIST111 surveys modern history and decolonisation but is organised mainly around European and international developments; GOSHIST211 treats empires comparatively; GOSHIST311 is explicitly Native American history in the United States; GOSHIST312 is a Walcheren Expedition research seminar. These do not form a modern Latin American history sequence. GOSPOLI112, GOSPOLI212, GOSPOLI312 and GOSPOLI313 provide comparative-politics, international-relations, general public-policy and peace/conflict frameworks; BENECON111, BENECON211, BENECON311 and BENECON312 provide economics, international macroeconomics, public economics and econometrics. They offer real analytic contributions but no sustained Latin American politics, economy, inequality, policy or geopolitics content. GOSSOCI111/214 address colonial context, GOSSOCI215 uses global environmental-justice cases, and GOSSOCI311 includes civil-repair cases in Latin America within a broader civil-society/decolonial course; this one direct regional segment cannot anchor a complete area-studies curriculum. HCBCOGN312 studies psycholinguistics and bilingualism and MCCCOMM211 stylistics, but neither teaches Spanish/Portuguese or Latin American sociolinguistics, language history, migration/contact and multilingualism as a regional sequence. MCCLITR111/211/311/312 and MCCMEDI111/212/311/312 teach literature, film, adaptation, postcolonial/Indigenous media, race and documentary methods; their documented corpora do not constitute Latin American literature, cinema, music or popular culture. No workbook row offers Spanish or Portuguese acquisition. Academic feasibility fails before accepting 24 courses, so no schedule or UCR-credit comparison is fabricated.

candidateAssessment.concept: Latin American histories, societies and political economy
candidateAssessment.assessment: UCR offers strong generic frameworks in modern/imperial history, comparative politics, international relations, sociology, economics and public policy. Only a limited part of one sociology course expressly uses Latin American civil-repair cases. That is insufficient to sustain a 23-course Latin America-centred progression in regional history, politics, economies, inequality and current developments.

Psycholinguistics and stylistics provide genuine language-analysis methods, but UCR offers neither Spanish nor Portuguese acquisition and no documented sequence in their history, Latin American language contact, regional multilingualism or language policy. A general cognitive-linguistics direction would change the stated object.

candidateAssessment.concept: Latin American literature, film and popular culture
candidateAssessment.assessment: Literary, film, media and communication courses provide useful analytic techniques, but their documented corpora and organising content are not Latin American literature, cinema, music, social media or popular culture. Generic method courses cannot fill a complete region-centred programme honestly.
